name: LLM_CHAT
description: A chat-completion model provider. One required action, `chat`: messages in, an assistant message (or a stream handle) out — or, when the turn failed in a way the provider can name (the vendor said no, or the provider declined the request), a `Failure` the caller can classify without reading error text. One optional action, `accepts`: what the provider takes under its `$config`, for a caller to ask before a turn. The wire shapes here are the harness's own, not any vendor's; a provider plugin translates them to its API. Prose contract in docs/SPI.md. Schemas are documentation and tooling input: Gwead validates no payloads at dispatch.

chat.description: One model turn. With `stream` unset or false the model's whole reply comes back as `message`; with `stream: true` the result instead carries an integer stream handle yielding newline-delimited JSON events shaped by `streamEventShape`, unless the provider declined the request before starting a stream, in which case it is the failed form.

system.description: System prompt. A top-level field, not a message: `messages` roles are only `user` and `assistant`.

messages.description: The conversation so far, oldest first.

tools.description: Tools the model may call this turn. Derived from TOOL plugins' manifests (the `tool` block of each action that carries one); absent or empty means no tools.

max_tokens.description: Cap on generated tokens. Optional; the provider applies its own default and ceiling.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature, in the provider's own scale: vendors differ on the range. Optional; absent means the provider's default. A provider that cannot honour the value answers with a `Failure` and never drops it. A provider that predates this field (before 0.8.0) may drop it without a word, so a caller that relies on it asks `accepts` first.

response_schema.description: A JSON Schema the answer is generated to. When `stop_reason` is `end_turn`, the text of the answer's text blocks, joined in order, is one JSON document conforming to it; other blocks are as without it, and a `max_tokens` or `refusal` stop carries no such guarantee. The output shapes do not change: streamed, the document arrives as `text` events. A provider that takes response schemas at all takes every schema within the floor docs/SPI.md names, and may refuse anything beyond it, or this field beside a non-empty `tools`, with a `Failure`; one that takes none refuses every schema with a `Failure`. Neither answers unconstrained text in its place. Nothing checks the document against the schema. A provider that predates this field (before 0.8.0) may drop it without a word, so a caller that relies on it asks `accepts` first.

stream.description: Ask for the streamed output form.

oneOf.description: The buffered form (`stream` false or absent).

stream.description: A Gwead stream handle: an index into the StreamRegistry the caller attached to this execution, meaningless against any other table (each table numbers its handles from 1; an execution run without a caller-supplied table has its streams drained when it returns). It yields UTF-8 newline-delimited JSON, one `streamEventShape` event per line, ending with an `end` event followed by end-of-stream. The assistant message a consumer rebuilds from the stream — to replay on the next turn — is the events in order, adjacent `text` events coalesced into one text block, `tool_use` and `opaque` events kept whole and in place. End-of-stream without an `end` event means the turn failed mid-stream — an `error` event, when the provider can still say why, is followed by end-of-stream, never by `end`.

oneOf.description: The failed form: the provider can say why the turn failed, as data. For instance, the vendor answered and said no (a non-2xx status, an error document), or the provider declined the request before calling a vendor (an image source it cannot resolve, a `temperature` or `response_schema` it cannot honour). On a streamed request it comes back in place of the stream handle only when the provider declined the request before starting a stream; once a stream exists, a failure is its `error` event. Failures the provider cannot classify without reading error text (the transport failed, the operator denied the egress, the kernel refused the step) stay step errors, which the caller treats as uniformly fatal to the turn.

accepts.description: What the provider takes under the `$config` it runs with, for a caller to decide before a turn what to offer. No input beyond `$config`. A provider without this action does not say, which a caller reads as unknown for every kind of input. A caller need not ask, and the answer binds the provider to nothing: a turn it cannot serve still answers with `chat`'s failed form.

output.description: One key per kind of input. A key that is absent means the provider does not know, which is distinct from `false`: a provider that can only find out from its server, and cannot, leaves the key out. Open on purpose: a later version adds a key for another kind of input, and a caller reads a key it does not know as nothing said. A known key whose value the schema does not admit is a contract violation, not an unknown.

images.description: Whether a message may carry `image` blocks, in a user message or in a `tool_result`'s content: `false` for none, or which ones.

temperature.description: Whether the provider honours `chat`'s `temperature`: `false` for no, or an object for yes.

response_schema.description: Whether the provider honours `chat`'s `response_schema`: `false` for no, or how.

oneOf.description: An increment of assistant text, to be concatenated in arrival order.

A complete tool call. Providers buffer partial tool-call deltas and emit the call whole: arguments are machine-consumed, so incremental display buys nothing and every consumer would otherwise reassemble JSON fragments.

A complete OpaqueBlock, emitted whole in its position among the turn's blocks. A consumer rebuilding the assistant message from the stream keeps it there, between the text and tool_use blocks around it.
The final event of every successful stream.

The turn failed and the provider can still say why. Always the last event: followed by end-of-stream, never by `end`. The same three fields as `Failure`, flattened beside `type`. `retryable` marks failures worth repeating unchanged (rate limit, overload) as opposed to ones that will fail again (bad credentials); absent means unknown. `kind` is a provider-specific identifier, informational only.

AssistantMessage.description: May be empty: a refusal, or `max_tokens` hit immediately, can stop a turn before any block completes. Replayed on later turns exactly as the provider produced it — opaque blocks included, in place.

OpaqueBlock.description: Provider state the consumer carries but never reads: a vendor's thinking block, say, which the vendor requires replayed verbatim in a later tool-use turn. Produced only by a provider, consumed only by a provider. A consumer keeps it in its position in the assistant message and replays it unchanged — never rendered, altered, reordered, or dropped — and makes no assumption about the shape of `data`. `provider` names the plugin that produced it, so a provider ignores blocks another produced.

ImageBlock.description: An image shown to the model, in its position among the blocks around it: a user message's, or a `tool_result`'s content. `source.type` says how the image travels: its bytes inline, or a reference the provider resolves.

data.description: The file's bytes in standard padded base64 (RFC 4648 section 4).

ReferenceImageSource.description: An image named by a reference in place of its bytes. The consumer stores and replays the reference unchanged and never interprets it; resolving it is the provider's. A provider that cannot resolve it answers with the failed form (`retryable` false) without calling a vendor. `media_type` is declared by whoever built the block, since the consumer has no bytes to read it from.

ImageMediaType.description: The image formats this contract names.

ImageInput.description: The images a provider takes. Open like the answer it sits in: a later version may add a field, and a caller ignores one it does not know.

sources.description: The source types it takes: `base64`, the bytes inline, and `reference`, a reference it resolves.

TemperatureInput.description: The provider honours a temperature. No fields at this version; open like the answer it sits in, so a later version may add one (a maximum, say).

ResponseSchemaInput.description: How the provider honours a response schema. Open like the answer it sits in.

with_tools.description: Whether it honours one beside a non-empty `tools`.

keywords.description: JSON Schema keywords it honours beyond the floor docs/SPI.md names, by name (`anyOf`, `$ref`); empty for the floor alone.

ToolUseBlock.description: The model asks for a tool. `id` is the provider's identifier for this call, echoed back by the matching ToolResultBlock; `input` is arguments per the tool's declared schema.

ToolResultBlock.description: A tool's result, carried back to the model in the next user message: a string, or a non-empty list of text and image blocks in order.

Tool.description: A tool offered to the model — a Gwead tool descriptor on the wire. `input_schema` is the JSON Schema for the call's arguments, taken verbatim from the TOOL plugin's `tool.parameters`.

StopReason.description: Why generation stopped: the model finished, the model wants tool results, `max_tokens` was hit, or the model declined to continue (a `refusal` turn must not be retried or continued). A consumer receiving a value outside this enum must treat the turn as failed; adding a value is therefore a contract change, never a quiet extension.

Failure.description: Why a turn failed, from a provider that can still say. `retryable` marks failures worth repeating unchanged (rate limit, overload, a transient server error) as opposed to ones that will fail again (bad credentials, a malformed request); absent means unknown. `kind` is the provider's own identifier for the failure class (an Anthropic `error.type`, say), informational only: consumers branch on `retryable`, never on `kind` or `message`.

Usage.description: Token accounting. Deliberately open: a provider may report extra counters (cache reads, for instance) under its own keys, and consumers must tolerate and may ignore them — only the two required fields are contractual.
